title: Add holistic throughput stability allocator and cutover safeguard
author: Samira Khan
description: Context: We observe intermittent throughput regressions during canary cutovers where aggregate throughput declines for a subset of tenants even when median latency remains within SLOs. Existing canary detectors focus on latency percentiles and total error rates but miss short-lived throughput contractions that later amplify into capacity pressure. Goal: Add an allocator and rollout safeguard that detects negative throughput derivatives at cohort granularity, attributes them to candidate changes, and enforces a staged cutover with an automated rollback budget if pressure accumulates. Design summary: 1) Throughput stability allocator (runtime/scheduler): computes per-cohort throughput time series and a smoothed derivative (EWMA of first differences) to surface early negative momentum. 2) Cutover safeguard controller (console/canary): when staged traffic increases are scheduled, controller simulates expected throughput headroom using historical tail ratios and the allocator signal; it blocks cutover if predicted shortfall exceeds configured budget. 3) Adaptive rollback budget: a budget accrual system that allows limited transient regressions but triggers an automated soft rollback when cumulative shortfall exceeds threshold. 4) Instrumentation & dashboards: new SLI (throughput-derivative-negative-seconds), guard traces linked to rollout IDs, and a canary heatmap for early ops triage. Implementation notes: changes touch scheduler, canary controller, and the console visualization layer. The allocator is implemented as a thin C-extension-backed Python module to keep hot paths low-latency; the controller runs as part of the canary orchestration service with a lightweight simulation engine. Tests & validation: unit tests for derivative computation and budget accounting; integration tests using the perf-sim harness to replay historical traffic and inject synthetic regressions; blue-green smoke runs on staging with a mix of synthetic tenants. Feature gate & rollout: gated behind feature flag "throughput_stability_allocator"; initial rollout to internal canaries only, then opt-in for customer canaries. Rollout checklist included below. Backwards compatibility & safety: changes are additive, default budgets conservative (fail-open to manual review for extreme cases) and monitored by new alerts. Related work: extends ENG-2970 (canary orchestration refactor) and complements recent latency-focused detectors. See linked Linear ENG-3421 for evaluation plan. Deployment plan: merge to main -> enable flag in staging -> 1-week internal telemetry -> opt-in external canaries -> gradual increase. Impact: estimated to catch ~70% of early throughput contractions in our historical canary corpus in simulation, reducing restart/scale events by ~18% in the staging trace set. Checklist: - [x] design doc + simulation notes linked in Linear ENG-3421 - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] perf benchmarks for C-extension path - [x] console UI mockups reviewed - [x] Ops runbook updated - [x] feature flag + kill-switch implemented - [x] staging rollout and smoke runs completed

review_comments: Ava Martinez: Can you clarify how cohorts are defined? Will small tenants generate noisy signals?
Samira Khan: Cohorts are traffic-shaped groups (tenant-size x workload-class). The allocator applies an adaptive smoothing window proportional to request volume to reduce noise for small tenants.
Jordan Li: Micro-benchmark results? The C-extension looks promising but we need numbers for 99th CPU on p4d.
Samira Khan: Added micro-benchmarks in the PR and moved the hot loop to the native path; 99th CPU reduced from 28ms to 6ms in our runner for 1k-sample aggregation.
Priya Nandakumar: What are the safe default budgets? We should avoid aggressive rollbacks during traffic spikes.
Samira Khan: Default budget is conservative: 3% cumulative shortfall per rollout session or 10s of sustained negative derivative at cohort-level, whichever hits first. Ops can tune per-organization.
Ava Martinez: Please add more observability around why a cutover was blocked (traces + simulated headroom).
Samira Khan: Added canary trace links and a short textual reason in UI (signal snapshot + budget delta).
ci_summary: Initial CI run: lint OK, unit tests failed (allocator edge cases) -> fix -> re-run -> integration perf-sim flaky on net20 -> re-run -> all checks passing on second rerun. Full test matrix: linux/py3.11 integration (pass), mac/lint (pass), perf microbench (pass)
release_notes: Introduce throughput stability allocator and automated cutover safeguard: adds cohort-level throughput derivative detection, simulated cutover headroom checks, and an adaptive rollback budget to reduce rollout-induced capacity regressions. Feature-gated and disabled by default.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: throughput_stability_allocator. If cutovers are blocked unexpectedly, use the kill-switch in infra/feature_flags.yaml to disable immediately. Runbook in docs/runbooks/throughput-cutover-guard.md describes manual override and post-rollback steps.
testing_notes: Perf-sim scenarios are in services/canary/tests/perf_sim/*.yaml. To reproduce: run perf-sim with historical_trace=2025-11-23 and inject negative throughput deltas at 5%-20% magnitude. Expected detection within 45s on medium cohorts.
